title: Locality after normalisation: digesting global entanglement
html:
Remark. Locality after normalisation: digesting global entanglement

Two computational operations seemingly contradict: single Hecke crossings obey Markov locality, yet composite braid evaluation via Gröbner–Shirshov reduction is non-local. Wenzl's product factorisation, recorded in prop:trace-locality-meets-gs-non-locality, reconciles them. The GS algorithm digests global entanglement into local coefficients; after digestion, the Markov trace factorises locally over the normal form. The process is therefore local after normalisation.
